## Natural history notes

A large rhinoceros beetle characterized by a glossy dark brown to black body, strong digging legs, and a short horn or raised projection on the head and pronotum. In Florida, Phileurus valgus is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine woods, forest edges, parks, and yards where rotting logs, stumps, and decaying wood are available. Adults and larvae live in decomposing wood and organic debris, helping recycle nutrients, while adults may also prey on other wood-inhabiting insect larvae and are sometimes attracted to lights.
